common_name: Pugster Pinker Butterfly Bush (Dwarf Compact Deep Pink Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; cut stems back hard in late winter to a few inches above the ground to maintain its tight, compact form.

directions: Pugster Pinker was bred by Proven Winners ColorChoice from the Spring Meadow Nursery breeding program as a deeper-colored companion to Pugster Pink, carrying the same stout, deer-resistant stems and full-sized, fragrant flowers on an unusually compact dwarf frame. Each bloom opens a rich, saturated pink with a small bright orange eye, held in dense clusters that cover the plant from early summer through frost with no deadheading required. Its low, dense habit of roughly 2 feet tall and wide fits containers and the front of borders where full-sized butterfly bush would overwhelm the space, and it draws butterflies and bees reliably once established. It tolerates heat and drought well and needs only a hard late-winter cutback to rebloom vigorously each season.

common_name: Pugster Indigo Butterfly Bush (Dwarf Compact Deep Blue Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade; prune stems back hard in early spring to about 8 inches to keep the dense dwarf shape and promote strong new flowering wood.

directions: Pugster Indigo is part of the Pugster series from Proven Winners and the Spring Meadow Nursery breeding program, pairing the series' signature stout, winter-hardy stems and oversized flower clusters with a deep indigo-blue flower color set off by silvery-green foliage. It blooms non-stop from early summer into autumn without deadheading and holds up to wind and rain better than older dwarf butterfly bush types thanks to its thick, sturdy branching. Slightly taller and more spreading than the smallest Pugster selections, it still stays compact enough for mixed borders and large containers while drawing abundant butterflies, bees, and hummingbirds. Prune hard each early spring, since it blooms on new wood, to keep the plant tidy and floriferous.

common_name: Flutterby Grande Peach Cobbler Butterfly Bush (Sterile Peach-Pink Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; cut back hard in late winter or early spring to a framework of a few buds to keep the shrub full and encourage the large, continuous flower spikes.

directions: Flutterby Grande Peach Cobbler was bred by Dr. Peter Podaras at Cornell University as part of the Flutterby Grande series, the first complete line of sterile, non-invasive butterfly bush selections, and it is sold under US Plant Patent protection through the Southern Living Plant Collection. It sets essentially no viable seed, so it will not escape into surrounding woods and fields the way older fertile Buddleja davidii selections can, making it a legal option in some jurisdictions that restrict butterfly bush. Large, dense flower panicles open a soft peach-pink over silvery-gray foliage and bloom continuously from midsummer to frost, drawing butterflies and hummingbirds in large numbers to a full-sized shrub reaching 4 to 6 feet. Give it full sun and a hard annual cutback for the strongest bloom.

common_name: Flutterby Grande Blueberry Cobbler Butterfly Bush (Sterile Violet-Blue Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; this is the largest Flutterby Grande selection, so allow ample room and cut back hard in late winter to control size and renew flowering wood.

directions: Flutterby Grande Blueberry Cobbler is another sterile Cornell-bred selection from Dr. Peter Podaras in the Flutterby Grande series, distributed through the Southern Living Plant Collection, and it produces almost no viable seed, limiting the escape risk associated with older fertile butterfly bush cultivars. It is the largest and most vigorous plant in the series, growing into a substantial, fountain-shaped shrub with long panicles of rich violet-blue flowers that bloom from midsummer through frost. Its size makes it well suited as a specimen, informal hedge, or back-of-border anchor where its continuous bloom can draw large numbers of butterflies and hummingbirds. Give it full sun, good drainage, and a hard late-winter pruning to manage its naturally large stature.

common_name: Flutterby Grande Tangerine Dream Butterfly Bush (Sterile Orange Silver-Leaved Buddleja Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; this hybrid tolerates heat and drought better than most davidii-type butterfly bush, so avoid overwatering, and cut back hard in late winter to maintain a dense form.

directions: Flutterby Grande Tangerine Dream is a sterile Buddleja marrubiifolia x Buddleja alternifolia hybrid from Dr. Peter Podaras's Flutterby Grande breeding program at Cornell University, marketed through the Southern Living Plant Collection, and it produces no viable seed, avoiding the self-sowing problem of older butterfly bush selections. Unlike most butterfly bush, its dense, silvery-gray foliage and compact clusters of warm orange flowers come from woolly butterfly bush parentage, giving it an unusually heat- and drought-tolerant constitution and a tidy, rounded form. It blooms from midsummer into fall, attracting butterflies and bees even in hot, dry summer conditions where typical Buddleja davidii selections may struggle. Give it full sun and sharp drainage, and prune hard in late winter to encourage dense new flowering growth.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

common_name: Flutterby Grande Vanilla Butterfly Bush (Sterile Creamy White Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; cut back hard in late winter or early spring to encourage the dense, continuous flowering typical of this series.

directions: Flutterby Grande Vanilla rounds out Dr. Peter Podaras's Cornell-bred Flutterby Grande series with a creamy white-flowered selection that, like its series mates, sets essentially no viable seed and will not spread into surrounding landscapes the way fertile old-fashioned butterfly bush can. Dense, fragrant flower spikes open a soft vanilla-white over gray-green foliage and bloom continuously from midsummer through the first hard frost, making it a bright contrast plant among the series' more saturated pinks, blues, and oranges. It grows into a full-sized, upright shrub well suited to borders, hedges, or specimen use where it reliably draws butterflies and other pollinators. Grow in full sun with good drainage and give it a hard annual cutback to maintain vigor and shape.
